[![GitHub](./assets/badges/github-badge.svg)](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS) [![License](./assets/badges/license-badge.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Demo](./assets/badges/demo-badge.svg)](https://edge0-ai.github.io/Audio8_TTS/realistic-0.6b/) [![arXiv](./assets/badges/arxiv-badge.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14776) [![Playground](./assets/badges/playground-badge.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b) [Languages](#supported-languages) · [Quick start](#installation) · [Serving](#high-throughput-serving-sglang-omni) · [Evaluation](#evaluation)
--- **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6B** builds on [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b), delivering **substantially improved speech realism** while retaining its compact **0.6B** architecture and zero-shot voice cloning capabilities. This release supports **23 languages**, adding **12 languages compared with Preview**. It uses the same Transformers inference interface as Preview. This repository includes the complete model checkpoint, its 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and custom Transformers code. Try speech generation and voice cloning in the [interactive Playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b). Hosted on Hugging Face ZeroGPU; availability depends on the queue and your daily GPU allowance. ## Highlights - **Improved realism:** more natural prosody and expressive delivery, building on Preview. - **Broader multilingual coverage:** 23 languages, including 12 additions to Preview's 11 supported languages. - **Compact model:** 601 million main-model parameters, with the audio codec bundled separately. - **Flexible generation:** zero-shot voice cloning from a reference recording and transcript, or speech generation without a reference. - **GPU serving:** an SGLang Omni adapter with paged attention, dynamic batching, and an OpenAI-compatible speech API. ## Supported Languages | Coverage | Languages | |---|---| | Supported in Preview (11) | Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish | | Added in Realistic (12) | Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese | > **Note:** Language quality varies; see the per-language evaluation below. Benchmark coverage includes some additional languages and is distinct from the supported-language list. ## Model Details Audio8 TTS uses a DualAR architecture inspired by [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech). The slow AR transformer predicts one semantic token for each audio frame. The fast AR transformer predicts the frame's codec codebooks, conditioned on the slow hidden state and preceding codebooks. | Component | Configuration | |---|---| | Main model | 601,159,424 parameters, excluding the codec | | Slow AR | 24 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Fast AR | 4 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Acoustic tokens | 10 codebooks, 4,096 entries per codebook | | Codec | 44.1 kHz, 2,048 samples per model frame (~21.5 frames/s) | | Context | Up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions | The bundled codec handles both reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding, so no additional codec checkpoint is required. The **0.6B** size refers to the main DualAR model; the codec is excluded from that parameter count. --- ## Installation Python 3.10 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended. ```bash pip install "torch>=2.5.0" "torchaudio>=2.5.0" \ "transformers>=4.57.0,<5" "soundfile>=0.12" "safetensors>=0.4" ``` The Transformers release package was smoke-tested with PyTorch 2.8.0 and Transformers 4.57.3 on an NVIDIA H20 using BF16. Checks covered model loading, English and Chinese generation with and without reference audio, and generation in Arabic, Cantonese, Portuguese, and Russian. These are runtime checks, separate from the benchmark results below. ## Usage The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the files in this repository, then load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Zero-shot voice cloning Use a clean reference recording. Its transcript must match the spoken content exactly. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["Welcome to Audio8 TTS. It is wonderful to hear from you."], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["The exact transcript of the reference recording."], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` ### Generation without a reference Replace the processor call above with: ```python inputs = processor( text=["This utterance does not use a reference voice."], return_tensors="pt", ) ``` Then move the inputs to the model device and run the same generation and decoding steps. For command-line inference, batching, and supervised fine-tuning, see the [Audio8 TTS repository](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS), using `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b` as the model path. ## High-throughput serving: SGLang Omni The [SGLang Omni adapter](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) provides GPU serving for Audio8 TTS. It is installed as an independent model plugin and does not overwrite SGLang Omni core files. | Capability | Support | |---|---| | Attention and batching | SGLang paged attention and dynamic batching | | DualAR execution | Slow AR serving with a fixed KV cache for the Fast AR codebook decoder | | Voice cloning | Reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding | | API | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` service | Use the **0.6B** configuration, `sglang_omni/configs/audio8_tts_0_6b.yaml`, and set the model path to `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b` or its downloaded snapshot. The adapter supports generation without a reference and zero-shot voice cloning. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS#sglang-omni-serving) for compatible dependency versions, installation, server configuration, and API examples. > **Validation note:** Audio8-TTS-Realistic was tested on an NVIDIA H20 in BF16 for generation with and without a reference through the non-streaming speech API, with Torch compilation and CUDA graphs disabled. These checks validate runtime compatibility; throughput and streaming were not benchmarked. --- ## Evaluation Error rates are percentages (**lower is better**). Speaker similarity (SIM) is on a **0–1 scale** (**higher is better**). These metrics measure intelligibility and speaker similarity; they do not directly measure perceived speech realism. ### Benchmark summary **Audio8-TTS-Preview** and **Audio8-TTS-Realistic**, both **0.6B**: | Benchmark | Coverage | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Seed-TTS | English / Chinese | 1.23 | 1.25 | 0.682 | 0.704 | | CV3 | 8 shared languages | 4.80 | 4.56 | — | 0.663 | | CV3 | 9 core languages | — | 4.86 | — | 0.661 | | MiniMax | 24 evaluated languages | — | 5.89 | — | 0.754 | > **Note:** Values are unweighted language macro averages. Preview results are calculated from its [published model card](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#evaluation), with SIM converted from percentages to a 0–1 scale. The two releases were evaluated separately. A dash means the corresponding result was not reported on Preview's card. > > Seed-TTS averages English WER and Chinese CER, excluding hard Chinese. The shared CV3 subset is Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, and Italian; the 9-language set also includes Russian. CV3 averages exclude hard subsets and the 13 additional languages. MiniMax averages all 24 evaluated languages, including languages outside the supported list. ### Reference comparison The following error rates come from the sources used in our technical report. Different evaluation pipelines and text normalization make this a reference comparison rather than a strictly matched ranking. A dash means that a result is unavailable in the comparison, not that the model lacks support. | Model | Parameters (B) | Seed-TTS EN/ZH error ↓ | CV3 (9) error ↓ | MiniMax (24) error ↓ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8-TTS-Realistic** | **0.6** | **1.25** | **4.86** | **5.89** | | Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B | 0.6 | 1.12 | — | — | | Qwen3-TTS-1.7B | 1.7 | 1.01 | 7.73 | 27.41 | | Higgs Audio v3 | 4 | 1.11 | 4.41 | 2.74 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7 | 1.17 | 4.49 | — | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6 | 1.32 | 4.49 | 4.40 | | MOSS-TTS-v1.5 | 8.5 | 1.52 | 6.11 | 3.78 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5 | 1.67 | 6.89 | — | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3 | 1.41 | 5.35 | — | > **Sources:** Qwen Seed-TTS results are from the Qwen3-TTS report, linked from the [official Qwen3-TTS repository](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS); Qwen's CV3/MiniMax results, all Higgs Audio v3 results, and MOSS-TTS-v1.5's CV3/MiniMax results are from [Boson AI's evaluation](https://huggingface.co/bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b). MOSS-TTS-v1.5's Seed-TTS result and the CosyVoice3/VoxCPM2 results are compiled in the [VoxCPM repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM). Listen to generated audio before using it in a finished product. - Obtain permission to clone a voice and disclose synthetic audio where appropriate. ## License and Acknowledgements The code and model weights are released under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). # KittenTTS 2

A 1.7B speech language model with in-context voice cloning. It reads text and writes S3
codec tokens, which a vocoder turns into 24 kHz audio.

```bash
pip install kittenml
```

```python
from kittenml import KittenTTS
import soundfile as sf

m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2")

# a built-in voice
audio = m.generate("Hi! umm.. how are you, I guess?  .. uh.. nice to meet you??",
                   voice="WeatherPresenterCheerful")

# or clone one, from 5-30 seconds of a single speaker
audio = m.generate("This is my own voice.", reference="my_voice.wav")

sf.write("output.wav", audio, m.sample_rate)
```

Everything the model needs is in this repository, so no Hugging Face login is required.

## Voices

`m.available_voices` lists all 115. Bella, Jasper, Luna, Bruno, Rosie, Hugo, Kiki
and Leo are the same speakers as in KittenTTS 0.8, so existing code keeps working.

Voices named after a person are English. The rest are named for the language they
speak followed by what they are — `SpanishAbuela`, `JapaneseTrainConductor`,
`RussianBabushka` — and are how you reach those languages, since the voice is what
carries the accent. Nine older entries carry a bare language name: Arabic, Chinese,
French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish.

```python
m.generate("Guten Morgen. Ich wünsche dir einen wunderschönen Tag.",
           voice="German", normalize=False)

m.generate("Buenas tardes. Hoy vamos a preparar algo muy especial.",
           voice="SpanishAbuela", normalize=False)
```

Sixteen languages have a named voice: Arabic, Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Hindi,
Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish,
and English.

Pass `normalize=False` for non-English text: the text normalizer is English-tuned and
will mangle numbers and dates in other languages.

## Expression controls

> **Beta.** Emotion control steers delivery rather than guaranteeing it, and the effect
> varies by voice and by sentence.

```python
m.generate("[joyful] We won the grant <laugh> I can (((hardly))) believe it!",
           voice="Kiki", preset="expressive")
```

A leading `[emotion]` tag, inline `<event>` tags and `(((emphasis)))` spans reach the
model as markup rather than being spoken, and switch on its expression conditioning.

**Emotions** — one leading tag sets the emotion for the whole line:

`[angry]` `[contemplative]` `[excited]` `[joyful]` `[mundane]`
`[nervous]` `[sad]` `[stern]` `[surprised]` `[tender]`

**Vocal events** — inline, anywhere in the line:

`<gasp>` `<giggle>` `<growl>` `<gulp>` `<laugh>`
`<pause>` `<scoff>` `<sigh>` `<sob>` `<um>`

**Emphasis** — triple parentheses stress a word or short phrase:

```python
m.generate("I told you (((never))) to open that door.", voice="Victor")
```

Only these twenty tags are recognised. They are the most common of the many in the
training data, so a rarer one such as `[reverent]` is spoken as ordinary text rather
than treated as markup — as is anything else bracketed, like `section [3]` or `x < 5`.

## Weight variants

The language model ships in three packings of the same weights. `weights=` picks one;
`model.available_weights` lists them.

| `weights=` | On disk | |
|---|---|---|
| `"packed"` *(default)* | 954 MB | 1.58-bit ternary body, bf16 embedding. **Lossless** |
| `"emb4"` | 469 MB | Same body in TL2, plus a 4-bit embedding. **Lossy** |
| `"full"` | 3469 MB | Plain bf16 |

```python
m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2", weights="emb4")
```

Only the variant you ask for is downloaded.

`emb4` halves the download, and the saving is almost entirely the token embedding — 324M
parameters that `packed` has to leave at bf16 because they are not ternary. Its transformer
body is still bit-exact: all 313 non-embedding tensors reproduce `full` exactly. The
embedding is not, at L2 relative error 0.118 against the bf16 export, and it is coded at
4.21 bits per weight across three frequency tiers. That is the one lossy thing here, which
is why `packed` stays the default.

## Decoders

Audio is decoded in two stages, and the first can be swapped for a smaller distilled
student with weights packed to 4 or 8 bits:

```python
m = KittenTTS("KittenML/kitten-tts-2", decoder="student_w4")
```

| Decoder | Flow on disk | |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | 459 MB | Best quality |
| `student_w4` | 39 MB | Distilled single-step student, weights packed to 4 bits |

These trade fidelity for footprint, not for speed: quantisation shrinks storage and
memory bandwidth, not arithmetic.

## What is in here

```
lm/          the speech language model, plus its spk_proj speaker head
speaker/     the speaker-embedding model used when cloning
voices/      reference clips, transcripts, and precomputed embeddings
decoders/    the optional 4-bit decoder
cpp/         GGUF weights for the llama.cpp fork, see "Running on CPU"
config.json  token layout, decode presets, voice and decoder indexes
```

The weights are 947 MiB: 910 MiB for the language model and 37 MiB for the decoder.
A load pulls those rather than the whole repository, and only the decoder you ask for.

The language model's linear weights are ternary — within every 128-wide group each
value is exactly one of `{-scale, 0, +scale}` — so bf16 spends 16 bits to say one of
three things. `lm/model-ternary.safetensors` packs them five trits to a byte, 1.6 bits
per weight, with each group keeping its scale at full precision:

| | |
|---|---|
| `lm/model.safetensors` | 3.47 GB, bf16 throughout |
| `lm/model-ternary.safetensors` | **0.95 GB**, the same weights, 3.6x smaller |

The packing is exact rather than approximate, so the two produce bit-identical audio.
`config.json` points `lm_packed` at the smaller file and that is what gets downloaded;
the full file stays for anything loading this with plain `transformers`.

## Running on CPU

KittenTTS 2 runs on CPU out of the box — `device` is auto-detected — but the fastest way
is [kitten-tts-2-cpp](https://github.com/KittenML/kitten-tts-2-cpp), our llama.cpp fork.
The `cpp/` directory here holds what it needs: the GGUF language model and its decoders.

## Requirements

Python 3.10 or later, and PyTorch.

## License

These weights are released under the [Stellon Labs Community License](LICENSE.md). Research,
non-commercial and limited commercial use are free of charge; the commercial grant ends once you
or your affiliates pass USD $1,000,000 in annual revenue or in total cumulative funding, at which
point you need a separate license from Stellon Labs. Distributing the weights, a derivative, or a
product built on them carries attribution requirements — see Section IV(a).

Two things in here are covered by their own terms instead: `speaker/`, the pyannote
speaker-embedding model, under [MIT](speaker/LICENSE), and the `kittenml` Python package that
loads this repository, under Apache 2.0.

--- license: other license_name: fish-audio-research-license license_link: LICENSE.md language: - ja base_model: fishaudio/s2-pro pipeline_tag: text-to-speech tags: - text-to-speech - japanese - voice-cloning - fish-audio - emotional-speech-generation - tts - speech - speech generation inference: false --- ![Iroha-TTS-V1 — an original anime character illustration for expressive Japanese TTS](assets/iroha-anime-hero-v2.png) # Iroha-TTS-V1 **Give every line a little more character.** Expressive Japanese TTS for character dialogue. Clone a voice, choose an emotion, adjust its intensity, and explore different takes on the same line. **Built with Fish Audio.** Based on [Fish Audio S2-Pro](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/s2-pro).
[Features](#features) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Parameters](#parameters) · [Agent guide](AGENT_GUIDE.md) · [中文](README_zh.md) ## Features ![One original anime character expressing joy, anger, sadness and surprise](assets/iroha-emotions-v2.png)

01 · Direct the emotion

Give one character joy, anger, sadness or surprise with a simple tag.

[happy] [angry] [sad] [surprised]

02 · Dial in the intensity

Choose one of four presets, or pass a float within the supported range to explore the space between them.

weakest → weak → default → strong
intensity=-0.015

03 · Turn the mood mid-line

Move from delight to sadness within one generation, without stitching separate audio clips.

[happy]やっと会えた。[sad]でも、もうお別れだね。

04 · Your voice, in character

Clone a voice from a short reference recording and its transcript, then explore different expressions.

Reference audio + transcript

05 · More than spoken words

Place laughter, sighs or crying where the scene calls for them.

[laugh] [sigh] [cry]

06 · Tell it in a whisper

Use a whisper tag for quiet dialogue and close-up moments.

[whisper]ここだけの話だよ。

07 · Give names their reading

Add kana to names, rare words and heteronyms to specify how they should be pronounced.

水神[すいじん] / 水神[みずかみ]
Intensity control is experimental: continuous coefficients do not imply a linear perceptual response. Crying, whispering and voice matching vary with the line and reference. The illustrations show expressions; the reference audio determines the voice. [Hear more scenes →](https://claude.ai/artifact/EnAFVuqrC4E6QA7BSVY7dg) ## Quick start Linux · Python 3.12 · NVIDIA GPU with at least 28 GB free VRAM. First use downloads about 11 GB of base weights. Run with an HF login that has access to this repository: ```bash python3.12 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -U huggingface_hub hf download IrohaStudio/Iroha-TTS --local-dir Iroha-TTS cd Iroha-TTS pip install -r requirements.txt python infer.py \ --text "やっと会えたね！ずっと待ってたんだよ。" \ --emotion joy --intensity -0.015 --seed 7 \ --ref my_voice.wav --ref-text "Exact transcript of the reference recording" \ --out joy.wav ``` Replace `my_voice.wav` and the reference text with your recording and its accurate transcript. Output is 44.1 kHz WAV. # Voxtral-Small-24B-2507: transcribe.cpp GGUF

GGUF conversions of [mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507) for use
with [transcribe.cpp](https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp).

Ported from upstream commit
[da5b424](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507/commit/da5b424),
pinned 2026-06-05.
Validated against the Transformers reference at transcribe.cpp commit
[dac22fa](https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp/tree/dac22fa)
on 2026-06-05.

Offline audio-LLM speech-to-text and speech translation. A Whisper-large-v3
bidirectional audio encoder feeds a 4-frame-group projector (375 audio tokens
per 30 s chunk) into a Mistral-Small-24B causal LM (40 layers, GQA 32/8, NEOX
RoPE, SwiGLU) via audio-token injection. Takes a 16 kHz mono WAV and produces a
transcript via greedy decoding. The larger sibling of Voxtral Mini 3B — same
encoder, projector, frontend, and tokenizer, with a scaled-up decoder.

## Usage

Build transcribe.cpp from source:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:handy-computer/transcribe.cpp.git
cd transcribe.cpp
cmake -B build && cmake --build build
```

```bash
build/bin/transcribe-cli \
  -m Voxtral-Small-24B-2507-Q8_0.gguf \
  input.wav
```

If your audio isn't already 16 kHz mono WAV, convert it first:

```bash
ffmpeg -i input.mp3 -ar 16000 -ac 1 output.wav
```

See the [transcribe.cpp model page](https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp/blob/main/docs/models/voxtral-small-24b-2507.md) for performance

# Voxtral Small 1.0 (24B) - 2507

Voxtral Small is an enhancement of [Mistral Small 3](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Base-2501), incorporating state-of-the-art audio input capabilities while retaining best-in-class text performance. It excels at speech transcription, translation and audio understanding.

Learn more about Voxtral in our blog post [here](https://mistral.ai/news/voxtral) and our [research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13264).

## Key Features

Voxtral builds upon Mistral Small 3 with powerful audio understanding capabilities.
- **Dedicated transcription mode**: Voxtral can operate in a pure speech transcription mode to maximize performance. By default, Voxtral automatically predicts the source audio language and transcribes the text accordingly
- **Long-form context**: With a 32k token context length, Voxtral handles audios up to 30 minutes for transcription, or 40 minutes for understanding
- **Built-in Q&A and summarization**: Supports asking questions directly through audio. Analyze audio and generate structured summaries without the need for separate ASR and language models
- **Natively multilingual**: Automatic language detection and state-of-the-art performance in the world’s most widely used languages (English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Hindi, German, Dutch, Italian)
- **Function-calling straight from voice**: Enables direct triggering of backend functions, workflows, or API calls based on spoken user intents
- **Highly capable at text**: Retains the text understanding capabilities of its language model backbone, Mistral Small 3.1

## Benchmark Results

## Usage

The model can be used with the following frameworks;
- [`vllm (recommended)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm): See [here](#vllm-recommended)
- [`Transformers` 🤗](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers): See [here](#transformers-🤗)

**Notes**:

- `temperature=0.2` and `top_p=0.95` for chat completion (*e.g. Audio Understanding*) and `temperature=0.0` for transcription
- Multiple audios per message and multiple user turns with audio are supported
- Function calling is supported
- System prompts are not yet supported


### vLLM (recommended)

We recommend using this model with [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm).

#### Installation

Make sure to install vllm >= `0.10.0`, we recommend using uv

```
uv pip install -U "vllm[audio]" --system
```

Doing so should automatically install [`mistral_common >= 1.8.1`](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-common/releases/tag/v1.8.1).

To check:
```
python -c "import mistral_common; print(mistral_common.__version__)"
```

#### Offline

You can test that your vLLM setup works as expected by cloning the vLLM repo:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm && cd vllm
```

and then running:

```sh
python examples/offline_inference/audio_language.py --num-audios 2 --model-type voxtral
```

#### Serve

We recommend that you use Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 in a server/client setting. 

1. Spin up a server:

```
vllm serve mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 --tokenizer_mode mistral --config_format mistral --load_format mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2 --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

**Note:** Running Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 on GPU requires ~55 GB of GPU RAM in bf16 or fp16. 


2. To ping the client you can use a simple Python snippet. See the following examples.


### Audio Instruct

Leverage the audio capabilities of Voxtral-Small-24B-2507 to chat.

Make sure that your client has `mistral-common` with audio installed:

```sh
pip install --upgrade mistral_common\[audio\]
```

<details>
  <summary>Python snippet</summary>

```py
from mistral_common.protocol.instruct.messages import TextChunk, AudioChunk, UserMessage, AssistantMessage, RawAudio
from mistral_common.audio import Audio
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

from openai import OpenAI

# Modify OpenAI's API key and API base to use vLLM's API server.
openai_api_key = "EMPTY"
openai_api_base = "http://<your-server-host>:8000/v1"

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=openai_api_key,
    base_url=openai_api_base,
)

models = client.models.list()
model = models.data[0].id

obama_file = hf_hub_download("patrickvonplaten/audio_samples", "obama.mp3", repo_type="dataset")
bcn_file = hf_hub_download("patrickvonplaten/audio_samples", "bcn_weather.mp3", repo_type="dataset")

def file_to_chunk(file: str) -> AudioChunk:
    audio = Audio.from_file(file, strict=False)
    return AudioChunk.from_audio(audio)

text_chunk = TextChunk(text="Which speaker is more inspiring? Why? How are they different from each other? Answer in French.")
user_msg = UserMessage(content=[file_to_chunk(obama_file), file_to_chunk(bcn_file), text_chunk]).to_openai()

print(30 * "=" + "USER 1" + 30 * "=")
print(text_chunk.text)
print("\n\n")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model,
    messages=[user_msg],
    temperature=0.2,
    top_p=0.95,
)
content = response.choices[0].message.content

print(30 * "=" + "BOT 1" + 30 * "=")
print(content)
print("\n\n")
# The model could give the following answer:
# ```L'orateur le plus inspirant est le président.
# Il est plus inspirant parce qu'il parle de ses expériences personnelles
# et de son optimisme pour l'avenir du pays.
# Il est différent de l'autre orateur car il ne parle pas de la météo,
# mais plutôt de ses interactions avec les gens et de son rôle en tant que président.```

messages = [
    user_msg,
    AssistantMessage(content=content).to_openai(),
    UserMessage(content="Ok, now please summarize the content of the first audio.").to_openai()
]
print(30 * "=" + "USER 2" + 30 * "=")
print(messages[-1]["content"])
print("\n\n")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model,
    messages=messages,
    temperature=0.2,
    top_p=0.95,
)
content = response.choices[0].message.content
print(30 * "=" + "BOT 2" + 30 * "=")
print(content)

#### Function Calling

Voxtral has some experimental function calling support. You can try as shown below.

Make sure that your client has `mistral-common` with audio installed:

```sh
pip install --upgrade mistral_common\[audio\]
```

Starting with `transformers >= 4.54.0` and above, you can run Voxtral natively!

Install Transformers:

from transformers import VoxtralForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor

repo_id = "mistralai/Voxtral-Small-24B-2507"

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(repo_id)
model = VoxtralForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(repo_id, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=device)

conversation = [

inputs = inputs.to(device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=500)
decoded_outputs = processor.batch_decode(outputs[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)

MOSS emits the diarized format `[start][Sxx]text[end]`; the bracket spans are metadata and are de-diarized to a space (for both hypothesis and reference) before scoring, matching the author-repo reference runner. The upstream card is the > authoritative source. # MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, diarization, timestamps, and acoustic event awareness. Given an audio or video file, the model generates a compact speaker-aware transcript in one pass, including timestamps and anonymous speaker labels such as `[S01]`, `[S02]`, and beyond. ## News * 2026-07-09: Released MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B. ## Contents - [Introduction](#introduction) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Evaluation](#evaluation) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Environment Setup](#environment-setup) - [Python Usage](#python-usage) - [Custom Prompt and Hotwords](#custom-prompt-and-hotwords) - [Serve with vLLM and SGLang](#serve-with-vllm-and-sglang) - [Subtitle Web App](#subtitle-web-app) - [Output Format](#output-format) - [More Information](#more-information) - [License](#license) - [Citation](#citation) ## Introduction MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B turns real-world long-form audio into structured, speaker-aware transcripts in one pass. Instead of stitching together separate ASR and diarization systems, it jointly performs speech transcription and speaker diarization, producing time-aligned text with consistent speaker labels. The model is built for meetings, calls, podcasts, interviews, lectures, videos, and other long or messy multi-speaker recordings. It can also emit acoustic event annotations, giving downstream systems a richer view of what happened, who spoke, and when. Core capabilities: * **Long-form transcription**: Converts long audio or video recordings into timestamped text. * **Speaker-aware diarization**: Assigns anonymous speaker labels such as `[S01]` and `[S02]` without a separate diarization pipeline. * **Promptable generation**: Supports custom transcription instructions, hotwords, and acoustic event annotations. ## Model Architecture

| Component | Specification | |---|---| | Text backbone | Qwen3-0.6B style causal decoder | | Audio encoder | Whisper-Medium encoder configuration | | Audio frontend | `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, 16 kHz, 80 mel bins, 30 s chunks | | Audio-text bridge | 4x temporal merge + MLP adaptor | | Fusion | Audio features replace <|audio_pad|> embeddings via `masked_scatter` | | Output format | Compact `[start][Sxx]text[end]` transcript with speaker tags such as `[S01]` | This Hugging Face repository includes the custom Transformers remote code required to load the model with `trust_remote_code=True`. ## Evaluation We evaluate MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize using three objective metrics: Character Error Rate (CER), concatenated minimum-permutation Character Error Rate (cpCER), and Delta-cp. Lower is better for all metrics. A dash (`-`) indicates that the result is unavailable.

## Quickstart ### Environment Setup Use a clean Python environment. The model uses custom Transformers code, so load the model and processor with `trust_remote_code=True`. ```bash conda create -n moss-transcribe-diarize python=3.12 -y conda activate moss-transcribe-diarize git clone https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize.git cd MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 torch torchaudio pip install -e . ``` The GitHub package provides helper utilities such as audio/video loading, transcription message construction, transcript parsing, CLI inference, and the subtitle web app. The model weights and remote-code model files are loaded from this Hugging Face repository. ### Python Usage ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor from moss_transcribe_diarize import parse_transcript from moss_transcribe_diarize.inference_utils import ( build_transcription_messages, generate_transcription, resolve_device, ) model_id = "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize" audio_path = "audio.wav" device = resolve_device("auto") dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device.type == "cuda" else torch.float32 model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype="auto", ).to(dtype=dtype).to(device).eval() processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, ) messages = build_transcription_messages(audio_path) result = generate_transcription( model, processor, messages, max_new_tokens=2048, do_sample=False, device=device, dtype=dtype, ) print(result["text"]) for segment in parse_transcript(result["text"]): print(segment.start, segment.end, segment.speaker, segment.text) ``` The message flow follows the common Qwen multimodal pattern: 1. `processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False)` renders text with audio placeholders. 2. The helper utilities load audio waveforms from the same messages. 3. `processor(text=text, audio=audios)` computes Whisper input features and expands audio placeholders. 4. `model.generate(...)` produces timestamped transcription and diarization text. ### Custom Prompt and Hotwords The default prompt is optimized for timestamped transcription and speaker diarization: ```text 请将音频转写为文本，每一段需以起始时间戳和说话人编号（[S01]、[S02]、[S03]…）开头，正文为对应的语音内容，并在段末标注结束时间戳，以清晰标明该段语音范围。 ``` To add hotwords, append a short hint to the default prompt: ```text 请将音频转写为文本，每一段需以起始时间戳和说话人编号（[S01]、[S02]、[S03]…）开头，正文为对应的语音内容，并在段末标注结束时间戳，以清晰标明该段语音范围。热词提示：热词1, 热词2, 热词3 ``` More prompt recipes are available in the GitHub repository: ### Serve with vLLM and SGLang MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize supports vLLM serving through the OpenAI-compatible transcription API. Use a pinned vLLM nightly build that includes the MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model registration. Choose one of the following commands: for CUDA 12 environments, use `cu129`; for CUDA 13 environments, use `cu130`. ```bash uv pip install -U vllm \ --torch-backend=auto \ --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/68b4a1d582818e67adc903bf1b8fc5a5447da2fa/cu129 ``` or: ```bash uv pip install -U vllm \ --torch-backend=auto \ --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/68b4a1d582818e67adc903bf1b8fc5a5447da2fa/cu130 ``` ```bash vllm serve OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize --trust-remote-code ``` ```bash curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model="OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize" \ -F file=@"audio.wav" \ -F response_format="json" \ -F temperature="0" ``` The recommended way to serve MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize is [SGLang Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni) through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint. Install `sglang-omni` by following the [installation guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/get_started/installation.md), then download the model: ```bash hf download OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize ``` Serve the model: ```bash sgl-omni serve \ --model-path OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ --port 8000 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 ``` Use `response_format=verbose_json` when you need parsed speaker segments. `json` returns the raw transcript text only. ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model=OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ -F file=@audio.wav \ -F response_format=verbose_json ``` ```python import requests with open("audio.wav", "rb") as f: resp = requests.post( "http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions", data={ "model": "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize", "response_format": "verbose_json", }, files={"file": ("audio.wav", f, "audio/wav")}, timeout=300, ) resp.raise_for_status() payload = resp.json() print(payload["text"]) for segment in payload.get("segments", []): print(f"[{segment['start']:.2f}-{segment['end']:.2f}] {segment['text']}") ``` For longer multi-speaker audio, raise `max_new_tokens` so the decoder can finish the full diarized transcript: ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model=OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ -F file=@audio.wav \ -F response_format=verbose_json \ -F max_new_tokens=65536 ``` | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `file` | file | required | Audio file uploaded as multipart form data | | `model` | string | server default | Model identifier | | `language` | string | unset | Optional language hint | | `response_format` | string | `json` | `json`, `verbose_json`, or `text` | | `temperature` | float | model default (`0.0`) | Sampling temperature | | `max_new_tokens` | int | `5120` | Max generated tokens; raise for long audio, for example `65536` | | `prompt` | string | unset | Optional instruction override; omit to use the built-in transcribe+diarize prompt | For benchmarking, performance numbers, and implementation details, see the [SGLang Omni cookbook](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/cookbook/moss_transcribe_diarize.md). The following single-H100 results are reported for short- and long-sequence multi-speaker ASR tasks. `movies` short-sequence ASR: | Concurrency | Throughput (req/s) | Mean latency (s) | RTF mean | audio_s/s | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 2.57 | 0.388 | 0.0612 | 29.76 | | 2 | 4.89 | 0.409 | 0.0659 | 56.55 | | 4 | 6.62 | 0.513 | 0.0790 | 76.64 | | 8 | 6.80 | 0.533 | 0.0810 | 78.70 | | 16 | 7.08 | 0.659 | 0.0922 | 81.98 | `aishell4_long` long-sequence ASR: | Concurrency | Throughput (req/s) | Mean latency (s) | RTF mean | audio_s/s | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.022 | 45.2 | 0.0197 | 50.64 | | 2 | 0.032 | 60.7 | 0.0265 | 74.25 | | 4 | 0.036 | 105.6 | 0.0461 | 81.64 | | 8 | 0.040 | 172.6 | 0.0754 | 90.62 | | 16 | 0.043 | 282.8 | 0.1237 | 98.83 | ### Subtitle Web App The source package includes a local subtitle workflow for upload, review, subtitle export, and optional FFmpeg burn-in: ```bash mtd-subtitle-web \ --model OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 7860 ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:7860`, upload an audio/video file, review the parsed subtitle segments, then download JSON/SRT/ASS or burn an MP4 if `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are available on `PATH`. For batch processing: ```bash mtd-subtitle /path/to/input.mp4 \ --model OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ --out-dir runs/example \ --render ``` ## Output Format The canonical output format is: ```text [start_time][Sxx]transcribed speech[end_time] ``` Example: ```text [0.48][S01]Welcome everyone[1.66][12.26][S02]The new transcription pipeline is ready for evaluation[13.81][14.36][S01]Great, include the diarization results in the report[18.76] ``` In this format: * `start_time` and `end_time` are timestamps in seconds. * `[S01]`, `[S02]`, and similar labels are anonymous model-generated speaker labels. * Speaker labels are relative labels within the input audio and should not be interpreted as real speaker identities. ## More Information * **GitHub**: * **MOSI.AI**: * **OpenMOSS**: ## License MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. ## Citation If you use MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B, please cite the technical report: ```bibtex @misc{moss_transcribe_diarize_2026, title={MOSS Transcribe Diarize Technical Report}, author={{MOSI.AI}}, year={2026}, eprint={2601.01554}, archivePrefix={arXiv}, primaryClass={cs.SD}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01554} } ```

[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-VoxCPM-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-ReadTheDocs-8CA1AF)](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live%20Playground-Demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenBMB/VoxCPM-Demo) [![Audio Samples](https://img.shields.io/badge/Audio%20Samples-Demo%20Page-green)](https://openbmb.github.io/voxcpm2-demopage) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-VoxCPM-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/KZUx7tVNwz) [![Lark](https://img.shields.io/badge/飞书群-VoxCPM-00D6B9?logo=lark&logoColor=white)](https://applink.feishu.cn/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=acds0b9d-23d8-4d7e-b696-d200f3e22a7f) [![MiniCPM Wiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/MiniCPM-Wiki-1677FF?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://modelbest.feishu.cn/wiki/UtWxwcERfiRIpIkBOjuc3h9tn1D) ## Highlights - 🌍 **30-Language Multilingual** — No language tag needed; input text in any supported language directly - 🎨 **Voice Design** — Generate a novel voice from a natural-language description alone (gender, age, tone, emotion, pace…); no reference audio required - 🎛️ **Controllable Cloning** — Clone any voice from a short clip, with optional style guidance to steer emotion, pace, and expression while preserving timbre - 🎙️ **Ultimate Cloning** — Provide reference audio + its transcript for audio-continuation cloning; every vocal nuance faithfully reproduced - 🔊 **48kHz Studio-Quality Output** — Accepts 16kHz reference; outputs 48kHz via AudioVAE V2's built-in super-resolution, no external upsampler needed - 🧠 **Context-Aware Synthesis** — Automatically infers appropriate prosody and expressiveness from text content - ⚡ **Real-Time Streaming** — RTF as low as ~0.3 on NVIDIA RTX 4090, and ~0.13 accelerated by [Nano-VLLM](https://github.com/a710128/nanovllm-voxcpm) - 📜 **Fully Open-Source & Commercial-Ready** — Apache-2.0 license, free for commercial use Supported Languages (30) Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Lao, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese Chinese Dialects: 四川话, 粤语, 吴语, 东北话, 河南话, 陕西话, 山东话, 天津话, 闽南话 ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install voxcpm ``` **Requirements:** Python ≥ 3.10, PyTorch ≥ 2.5.0, CUDA ≥ 12.0 · [Full Quick Start →](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html) ### Text-to-Speech ```python from voxcpm import VoxCPM import soundfile as sf model = VoxCPM.from_pretrained("openbmb/VoxCPM2", load_denoiser=False) wav = model.generate( text="VoxCPM2 brings multilingual support, creative voice design, and controllable voice cloning.", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("output.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Voice Design Put the voice description in parentheses at the start of `text`, followed by the content to synthesize: ```python wav = model.generate( text="(A young woman, gentle and sweet voice)Hello, welcome to VoxCPM2!", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("voice_design.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Controllable Voice Cloning ```python # Basic cloning wav = model.generate( text="This is a cloned voice generated by VoxCPM2.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", ) sf.write("clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) # Cloning with style control wav = model.generate( text="(slightly faster, cheerful tone)This is a cloned voice with style control.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("controllable_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Ultimate Cloning Provide both the reference audio and its exact transcript for maximum fidelity. Pass the same clip to both `reference_wav_path` and `prompt_wav_path` for highest similarity: ```python wav = model.generate( text="This is an ultimate cloning demonstration using VoxCPM2.", prompt_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", prompt_text="The transcript of the reference audio.", reference_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", ) sf.write("hifi_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Streaming ```python import numpy as np chunks = [] for chunk in model.generate_streaming(text="Streaming is easy with VoxCPM!"): chunks.append(chunk) wav = np.concatenate(chunks) sf.write("streaming.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ## Model Details | Property | Value | |---|---| | Architecture | Tokenizer-free Diffusion Autoregressive (LocEnc → TSLM → RALM → LocDiT) | | Backbone | Based on MiniCPM-4, totally 2B parameters | | Audio VAE | AudioVAE V2 (asymmetric encode/decode, 16kHz in → 48kHz out) | | Training Data | 2M+ hours multilingual speech | | LM Token Rate | 6.25 Hz | | Max Sequence Length | 8192 tokens | | dtype | bfloat16 | | VRAM | ~8 GB | | RTF (RTX 4090) | ~0.30 (standard) / ~0.13 (Nano-vLLM) | ## Performance VoxCPM2 achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on major zero-shot and controllable TTS benchmarks. See the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM#-performance) for full benchmark tables (Seed-TTS-eval, CV3-eval, InstructTTSEval, MiniMax Multilingual Test). ## Fine-tuning VoxCPM2 supports both full SFT and LoRA fine-tuning with as little as 5–10 minutes of audio: ```bash # LoRA fine-tuning (recommended) python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_lora.yaml # Full fine-tuning python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_all.yaml ``` See the [Fine-tuning Guide](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/finetuning/finetune.html) for full instructions. ## Limitations - Voice Design and Style Control results may vary between runs; generating 1–3 times is recommended to obtain the desired output. - Performance varies across languages depending on training data availability. - Occasional instability may occur with very long or highly expressive inputs. - **Strictly forbidden** to use for impersonation, fraud, or disinformation. AI-generated content should be clearly labeled. ## Citation ```bibtex @article{voxcpm2_2026, title = {VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning}, author = {VoxCPM Team}, journal = {GitHub}, year = {2026}, } @article{voxcpm2025, title = {VoxCPM: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Context-Aware Speech Generation and True-to-Life Voice Cloning}, author = {Zhou, Yixuan and Zeng, Guoyang and Liu, Xin and Li, Xiang and Yu, Renjie and Wang, Ziyang and Ye, Runchuan and Sun, Weiyue and Gui, Jiancheng and Li, Kehan and Wu, Zhiyong and Liu, Zhiyuan}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.24650}, year = {2025}, } ``` ## License Released under the [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) license, free for commercial use. For production deployments, we recommend thorough testing and safety evaluation tailored to your use case.

# Drama 3 8-bit, paged for gbx-lm

**Built with Fish Audio.** [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3), the expressive multi-speaker text-to-speech model, packaged for [gbx-lm](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm) on Apple silicon: an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` server that streams audio, and runs on Macs that cannot hold the whole model in memory.

This is a community build by GreenBitAI. It is not made, sponsored or endorsed by Fish Audio.

- **Where the weights come from.** Fish Audio's release, as converted to MLX by [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit), whose routed experts are 8-bit. Here the layers it kept in bfloat16 are 8-bit too, in the same format: a quarter faster, with speech quality unchanged within what we can measure (below). The routed experts live in `experts.bin`, one record per expert, so that a machine can read just the experts it needs. [NOTICE](NOTICE) lists every change.
- **Real time on 64 GB and up.** 56-58 frames per second on an M3 Ultra, 2.6x real time, first audio in under 0.3 s when streaming.
- **Runs on 32-48 GB, for offline use.** With less memory the experts stream from the SSD: up to three quarters of real time on a 48 GB Mac Studio and about half on a 48 GB MacBook Pro. Generate the file, then play it.

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | Apple silicon Mac, 64 GB or more for real time, 32 GB at least; or a DGX Spark |
| Disk | 40 GB for the model (37 GiB) |
| gbx-lm | v0.8.5 or later |
| Python | 3.10 or newer, for the audio codec (below) |

gbx-lm generates the model's audio *codes*; turning codes into sound is the job of a small companion package, [gbx-codecs](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-codecs), which gbx-lm starts in its own process. It needs only `mlx` and `numpy` -- no PyTorch, no ffmpeg -- and about 3 GB of memory while it decodes. The codec weights are in this repository.

## Setup

**1. gbx-lm.** The prebuilt binary, as in the [gbx-lm README](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm):

```bash
# upgrading? clear the previous version's unpack directory first
rm -rf ~/.libra/cache/onefile/gbx_lm

curl -fL -o gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz 'https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm/releases/latest/download/gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz' \
  && tar -xzf gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz gbx_lm \
  && mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" \
  && mv gbx_lm "$HOME/.local/bin/gbx_lm" \
  && chmod +x "$HOME/.local/bin/gbx_lm"
```

This replaces an older `gbx_lm` in `~/.local/bin`. Every version unpacks into the same `~/.libra/cache/onefile/gbx_lm`, and macOS stops a binary that finds another version's files there with `Killed: 9`: keep one version installed, and run the `rm -rf` line again whenever you switch.

**2. The codec**, in a virtual environment of its own (this location is the one gbx-lm looks in by default):

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/.gbx-codecs
~/.gbx-codecs/bin/pip install gbx-codecs
```

**3. Voices (optional).** To speak in a particular voice, put a short clean recording (5-30 s, WAV; flac and mp3 need `pip install "gbx-codecs[formats]"`) and its exact transcript side by side in a folder:

```
~/voices/
    narrator.wav
    narrator.txt      # the words spoken in narrator.wav
```

The request's `voice` is the file name, `narrator`. Use only voices you have the right to use -- see [License](#license). Without a voice (`"voice": "default"`) the model chooses one; fix it with a `seed`.

On a **DGX Spark** (or another Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU), use the Linux build of gbx-lm and install the codec with the CUDA build of MLX: `~/.gbx-codecs/bin/pip install "mlx[cuda13]" gbx-codecs`. The model runs in memory there, at about 1.4x real time.

**4. Start the server.** The model downloads on first start:

```bash
gbx_lm --model GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged --voices_dir ~/voices
```

If the codec is not in `~/.gbx-codecs`, add `--codec_python /path/to/that/python`. To check the codec on its own once the model is downloaded:

```bash
~/.gbx-codecs/bin/gbx-codecs check ~/.libra/cache/models/hub/models--GreenBitAI--Drama-3-8bit-paged/snapshots/*/
```

## Use

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:11688/v1/audio/speech -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged",
  "input": "[sighs] Fine. If we miss the train, that is on you. [laughs] Okay, okay, I am going.",
  "voice": "narrator",
  "response_format": "wav"
}' -o out.wav
```

With the OpenAI SDK, streaming as it is generated:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11688/v1", api_key="local")
with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
    model="GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged",
    voice="narrator",
    input="<|speaker:0|> Are you coming tonight? <|speaker:1|> I wouldn't miss it.",
    response_format="pcm",                # 24 kHz, 16-bit, mono
    extra_body={"stream_format": "audio", "seed": 7},
) as response:
    for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
        ...                               # play or write it
```

| field | |
|---|---|
| `input` | the text. Inline cues such as `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, `[whispering]`; speakers `<|speaker:0|>` to `<|speaker:15|>`. Long text is split and spoken in order |
| `voice` | a name from `--voices_dir`, or `default` |
| `response_format` | `wav` (44.1 kHz, the default) or `pcm` (24 kHz, as OpenAI's). Other formats are refused |
| `stream_format` | `audio` to stream; absent, the whole file is returned |
| `seed`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `sample_rate` | extensions; from the OpenAI SDK, pass them in `extra_body` |

`speed` other than 1.0 and `instructions` are refused (gbx-lm v0.8.5 ignored `instructions`): emotion and delivery come from the inline cues.

Keep one language to a request. With the `default` voice, a request that changes language part-way carries the first language's accent into the rest; split it into one request per language, or use a reference voice that speaks the language.

Pauses longer than a second are shortened in the output: the model occasionally goes silent mid-sentence for many seconds before finishing it.

## Quality

32 texts in English and Chinese (plain, cued, two-speaker, and long enough to be split), transcribed by Whisper large-v3-turbo:

| | English word error | Chinese character error |
|---|---|---|
| mlx-audio reference implementation, mlx-community weights (one take each) | 0.0% | 1.1-1.5% |
| this repository on gbx-lm (three takes each) | 0.0-2.9%, mean 1.2% | 1.1-1.9%, mean 1.5% |
| mlx-community weights on gbx-lm (three takes each) | 0.0-0.4%, mean 0.2% | 1.3-7.8%, mean 3.7% |

Single takes occasionally drop the end of a line -- in both builds, 1-2 takes in 96 -- so retry with another seed when one does. With experts streamed from disk the output is the same as in memory up to rounding.

## Speed

M3 Ultra, experts read from a cold SSD where they stream; the model makes 21.5 frames for each second of audio:

| Mac | how | frames/s | x real time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 GB and up | in memory | 56-58 | 2.6-2.7 |
| 48 GB | streaming experts | 15.5-17 | 0.7-0.8 |
| 32 GB | streaming experts | 10-11.5 | 0.5 |
| 48 GB MacBook Pro (M4 Pro) | streaming experts | 7.5-13 | 0.35-0.6 |

The Mac Studio's smaller tiers are measured with the expert cache gbx-lm would give those Macs, on the Studio's SSD; a laptop's is slower, as the MacBook Pro row shows. When the experts stream, the first request after the server starts takes 20-30 s before any audio while the expert cache fills, and later streamed requests start in about 3 s; first audio in 0.3 s needs the model in memory. 24 GB Macs can load the model and run at about a third of real time. gbx-lm decides how to load the model from the memory it finds; `GBX_PAGING=off` forces it into memory.

The [Fish Audio Community License, Version 1.0](LICENSE) applies to this model, including the outputs you make with it. In short, and the license itself governs:

Above that, or to offer text-to-speech to third parties as a **hosted service** (an API or app whose purpose is speech generation from their text or voices), you need a separate license from Fish Audio (business@fish.audio).
- Do not generate speech imitating an identifiable person without their consent, impersonate anyone to deceive, or use the outputs to train other speech or foundation models.
- [NOTICE](NOTICE) records the attribution and every change made to Fish Audio's weights, including this repository's.

gbx-lm is Apache 2.0 and gbx-codecs is MIT. The codec implementation in gbx-codecs and the model implementation in gbx-lm are adapted from [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) (MIT).

## Credits

Fish Audio for Drama 3. [cguldogan](https://github.com/cguldogan) for the MLX 8-bit conversion published as mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit. Prince Canuma and the mlx-audio contributors for the MLX implementation this build and its codec are based on.

The model was trained on [`xtts-egyptian-dataset-v2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullah-khaled/xtts-egyptian-dataset-v2), a single-speaker Egyptian Arabic corpus, and supports reference-audio-based voice conditioning like the original XTTS-v2. > ⚠️ **Research and experimental use only. Not for production.** > This is an experimental checkpoint. It has not been evaluated for robustness, safety, or reliability, and it must **not** be used in production systems, commercial products, or any setting where errors or misuse could cause harm. --- ## Model Summary | Property | Value | |---|---| | **Base model** | [`coqui/XTTS-v2`](https://huggingface.co/coqui/XTTS-v2) | | **Task** | Text-to-Speech (with reference-audio conditioning) | | **Target language** | Egyptian Arabic (use language code `ar`) | | **Fine-tuning data** | [`abdullah-khaled/xtts-egyptian-dataset-v2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullah-khaled/xtts-egyptian-dataset-v2) (single speaker, 22.05 kHz) | | **Output sample rate** | 24,000 Hz | | **Framework** | Coqui TTS (`XttsConfig` / `Xtts`) | | **Status** | Experimental research checkpoint | --- ## 🔊 Audio Sample Listen to a sample generated by this model: **Input text:** الماء مهم جداً لجسم الإنسان. [⬇️ Download `output.wav`](output.wav) > Generated with the settings listed in [Recommended generation settings](#recommended-generation-settings). The sample is provided for research demonstration only and quality may vary between runs and reference clips. --- ## Repository Files | File | Description | |---|---| | `model.pth` | Fine-tuned model weights | | `config.json` | XTTS model configuration | | `vocab.json` | Tokenizer vocabulary | | `output.wav` | Audio sample generated by the model | --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Install dependencies ```bash pip install coqui-tts torch torchaudio huggingface_hub ``` > `coqui-tts` is the maintained fork of Coqui TTS. The original `TTS` package also exposes the same `TTS.tts.models.xtts` modules, but may need older dependency versions. ### 2. Run inference You need a **reference audio file** (`reference.wav`): clean, mono, roughly 6–30 seconds of speech. The model uses it to compute the conditioning latents. ```python import os import torch import torchaudio from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download from TTS.tts.configs.xtts_config import XttsConfig from TTS.tts.models.xtts import Xtts # Download the model (log in first with `huggingface-cli login` # if the repository is private) d = snapshot_download("abdullah-khaled/xtts-egyptian-arabic", token=True) # Device device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" if device == "cpu": torch.set_num_threads(os.cpu_count()) # XTTS on CPU is slow # Load model config = XttsConfig() config.load_json(f"{d}/config.json") model = Xtts(config) model.load_checkpoint( config, checkpoint_dir=d, checkpoint_path=f"{d}/model.pth", vocab_path=f"{d}/vocab.json", use_deepspeed=False, ) # NOTE: .to() and .eval() return None for XTTS -- do not chain or reassign. model.to(device) model.eval() # Conditioning latents from a reference clip gpt_cond_latent, speaker_embedding = model.get_conditioning_latents( audio_path=["reference.wav"], gpt_cond_len=6, max_ref_length=30, sound_norm_refs=False, ) # Synthesize out = model.inference( text="الماء مهم جداً لجسم الإنسان.", language="ar", gpt_cond_latent=gpt_cond_latent, speaker_embedding=speaker_embedding, temperature=0.65, repetition_penalty=5.0, top_k=50, length_penalty=1.0, enable_text_splitting=True, # auto-splits long text ) # Save (XTTS-v2 outputs 24 kHz audio) torchaudio.save("output.wav", torch.tensor(out["wav"]).unsqueeze(0), 24000) ``` ### Recommended generation settings These are the settings used in the example above and a reasonable starting point: | Parameter | Value | Notes | |---|---|---| | `language` | `"ar"` | XTTS has no dedicated Egyptian code; Full details are in the [dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullah-khaled/xtts-egyptian-dataset-v2). - **Hyperparameters, epochs, hardware:** _Add your training details here (e.g., learning rate, batch size, number of epochs/steps, GPU)._ --- ## Intended Use & Restrictions ### ✅ Permitted - Academic and non-commercial research on Arabic / Egyptian-dialect speech synthesis - Personal experimentation, demos, and benchmarking - Educational use and reproducibility studies ### ❌ Not permitted - **Production deployment** of any kind - **Commercial use**, including paid products, APIs, or monetized content - Cloning or imitating a real person's voice **without their explicit consent** - Impersonation, fraud, deepfakes, misinformation, or harassment - Presenting synthetic speech as genuine human speech without disclosure Because this model is built on XTTS-v2, it also inherits the terms of the [Coqui Public Model License (CPML)](https://coqui.ai/cpml), which restricts commercial use. # Silencio-2

**Small English text-to-speech with emotions, sounds and voice cloning.**

Silencio-2 turns English text into 24 kHz speech in any voice, from a few seconds of reference audio.
You direct it inside the text: put `[sigh]` where a sigh belongs and `<whisper>` where the delivery changes.
It runs about 20x faster than real time on four CPU threads of an Apple M4, and all weights fit in one 112 MB file.

```python
tts.generate("What a long day. [sigh]")
tts.generate("<whisper> Keep your voice down.")
```

Silencio-2 is a fine-tune of [Pocket TTS](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts) 18M by Kyutai, retrained on a
custom dataset to follow tags. It has its own inference package, `silencio2`, so `pip install pocket-tts` is not needed.

[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1d6GSiRgXbYyBo91DCMrSr5y2LR_peJKy?usp=sharing)

## Tags

| Sounds, placed where they happen | Emotions, apply to the text after them |
|---|---|
| `[laugh]` `[sigh]` `[gasp]` `[cough]` `[clear_throat]` | `<happy>` `<sad>` `<angry>` `<fear>` `<surprised>` `<whisper>` |

An unknown tag raises an error instead of being read aloud.

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Run this from a clone of the repo, or add the snapshot folder to `sys.path`:

```python
from silencio2 import Silencio2TTS

tts = Silencio2TTS.from_pretrained()  # or a local folder; add quantize=True for int8 on CPU

# A bundled voice
tts.save("hello.wav", "Hi, I'm Silencio.", voice="260")

# Sounds go right into the text
tts.save("sigh.wav", "What a long day. [sigh]")

# An emotion for the whole text, or several inside it: each holds until the next one
tts.save("happy.wav", "We did it, we actually won!", emotion="happy")
tts.save("mixed.wav", "<whisper> Keep your voice down. <angry> I said stop!")

# Any voice from a short clean clip
tts.save("clone.wav", "Hi! This is my voice.", voice="my_clip.wav")

# Streaming: float32 chunks at tts.sample_rate
for chunk in tts.stream("A longer text, played as it is generated."):
    ...

wav = tts.generate("The same line, the same take.", seed=7)  # a 1-D float32 tensor
```

`generate` raises quiet takes to speech level, since a true whisper comes out about ten times quieter than speech.
Pass `normalize=False` to keep the raw level. `stream` does not change the level.

Bundled voices: `1320`, `2094`, `260`, `3575`, `5639`, `6930`, `7127`, `7729` (`tts.voices`).

## Samples

| Text | Audio |
|---|---|
| `Hi, I'm Silencio.` | [hi.wav](samples/hi.wav) |
| `What a long day. [sigh]` | [long_day_sigh.wav](samples/long_day_sigh.wav) |
| `<whisper> Keep your voice down.` | [whisper.wav](samples/whisper.wav) |
| `Hi! This is my voice.` (voice 7729) | [cloned_voice.wav](samples/cloned_voice.wav) |
| `[sigh] Finally... a voice that breathes.` | [finally_sigh.wav](samples/finally_sigh.wav) |

## Model details

- **Model type:** a flow-based language model that predicts latents of the Mimi codec from text and a voice prompt, one step per frame.
- **Size:** 27.9M parameters in `model.safetensors`: 18.2M generate speech, and the rest is the Mimi encoder that voice cloning needs.
- **Audio:** 24 kHz mono, streamed as it is generated.
- **Language:** English.
- **Text:** a sentencepiece tokenizer with 11 extra tokens, one per tag.

## How it was made

We extended the Pocket TTS 18M tokenizer and text table with the tag tokens, then fine-tuned the model on a custom dataset
with Kyutai's training code. A tag was removed from a fifth of the training texts, and the voice prompt of tagged clips was
often a neutral take of the same voice, so that the tag, not the prompt, sets the delivery. A final distillation stage bakes classifier-free
guidance into the weights, so inference needs one pass per frame.

## Limitations

- The delivery changes from take to take: try a few seeds. The same tag can come out strong in one take and faint in another.
- `<whisper>` is the least steady tag. It works best on short lines, and varies by voice.
- Check important lines by ear.
- English only.

## Responsible use

Clone a voice only with its owner's permission. Do not use Silencio-2 to impersonate people or to deceive. Say that speech is synthetic where listeners could take it for real.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `model.safetensors` | the weights |
| `tokenizer.model` | the tokenizer with the tag tokens |
| `config.yaml` | the model configuration |
| `silencio2/` | the inference package; `silencio2/core` is adapted from Pocket TTS |
| `voices/` | reference clips of the bundled voices |
| `samples/` | the samples above |
| `NOTICE.md` | third-party notices |

# Drama 3 MLX bf16

**Built with Fish Audio.**

[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) converted for [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) on Apple Silicon, with nothing quantized. This is an unofficial community conversion; Fish Audio did not release or endorse it.

Converted from the updated weights Fish Audio released on 2026-10-29 ([revision 78e5ab7](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3/tree/78e5ab79e49aa9a25abe8799eff2c4d73a1c3216)). The conversion of the first release stays at [revision d947126](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-bf16/tree/d947126c6a85861382a89ba54067b1af0a1cd6e2) of this repo.

- routed experts: dequantized from the block-FP8 release to bfloat16
- every other weight: bfloat16, as released
- 67 GB on disk, about 74 GB peak memory while generating, so it needs a Mac with at least 96 GB

For smaller Macs, [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-4bit](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-4bit) needs about 26 GB.

## Usage

Use mlx-audio 0.6.2 or later, which samples Drama 3 with SGLang-Omni's defaults:

```bash
pip install -U "mlx-audio>=0.6.2"
```

```python
from mlx_audio.tts.utils import load_model

model = load_model("mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-bf16")

for result in model.generate(
    text="[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it's on you.",
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    ref_text="Transcript of the reference clip.",
    stream=True,
    first_chunk_frames=4,
):
    print(result.audio.shape)  # 44.1 kHz chunks
```

```bash
python -m mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-bf16 \
    --text "[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it's on you." \
    --ref_audio reference.wav --ref_text "Transcript of the reference clip."
```

Speaker tags (`<|speaker:0|>` to `<|speaker:15|>`), multiple references and streaming are described in the [model docs](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio/blob/main/docs/models/tts/fish-drama3.md).

## Speed

On an M3 Max with 128 GB:

- about 1.4x real time
- first streamed audio in 270 to 300 ms once a voice is cached
- loading takes about 12 s from a warm page cache, and the first call after loading about 3 s

## Conversion

Made from fishaudio/drama-3 at [revision 78e5ab7](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3/tree/78e5ab79e49aa9a25abe8799eff2c4d73a1c3216) with mlx-audio's converter, with nothing quantized:

```bash
python -m mlx_audio.tts.models.fish_drama3.convert --src drama-3 --dst drama-3-mlx-bf16 \
    --expert-bits 0 --dense-bits 0 --tower-bits 0
```

`NOTICE` lists every change to the original weights.

# Audio8-TTS-Kurdish-Sorani

A **Central Kurdish (Sorani)** fine-tune of Audio8 TTS, a 0.6B-parameter DualAR text-to-speech model with zero-shot voice cloning. Neither Central Kurdish nor Persian is among the base model's supported languages. Training started from the Persian fine-tune [ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Persian](https://huggingface.co/ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Persian), whose script Sorani largely shares. <!-- If you trained from the original Audio8 (INIT_MODEL = "base"), change this sentence and base_model above to Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b. -->

Training code, Colab notebook and documentation: **https://github.com/ard9/Audio8-Persian-TTS**

> **Non-commercial use only.** The training data, [central-kurdish-tts4all](https://huggingface.co/datasets/aranemini/central-kurdish-tts4all), is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so this model is released under **CC BY-NC 4.0**: free for research, education and non-commercial demos; not for paid products or services.

## 🔊 Samples

| Text | Audio |
|---|---|
| سڵاو، ئەمڕۆ کەشوهەوا زۆر خۆشە و دەمەوێت کەمێک لە پارک پیاسە بکەم. | [ft_s01.wav](samples/ft_s01.wav) |
| دوێنێ لەگەڵ هاوڕێکانم چووین بۆ سینەما، فیلمەکە بەڕاستی زۆر جوان بوو! | [ft_s03.wav](samples/ft_s03.wav) |
| Voice clone (reference from another speaker of the dataset) | [clone_s01.wav](samples/clone_s01.wav) |

## Usage

The model uses Audio8's custom Transformers code (`trust_remote_code=True`). Normalize the text with the same Sorani rules as in training (`normalize_ckb` in the GitHub repo: Arabic letter variants unified, numbers spelled out in Kurdish).

```python
# pip install "transformers>=4.57,<5" soundfile
# git clone https://github.com/ard9/Audio8-Persian-TTS  (for fa_tools.normalize_ckb)
import sys, torch, soundfile as sf
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor
sys.path.insert(0, "Audio8-Persian-TTS/src")
from fa_tools import normalize_ckb

model_id = "ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Kurdish-Sorani"
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype).eval().to(device)

text = normalize_ckb("سڵاو! چۆنی؟")
inputs = processor(text=[text], return_tensors="pt")
# Voice cloning: add reference_audio=["ref.wav"], reference_text=[normalize_ckb("exact transcript")]
inputs = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in inputs.items()}
with torch.inference_mode():
    out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50,
                         do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True)
    wav, lengths = model.decode_audio(out.codes)
sf.write("output.wav", wav[0, : int(lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy(), model.config.codec_sample_rate)
```

Or from the command line: `python scripts/synthesize.py --model ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Kurdish-Sorani --lang ckb --text "سڵاو" --output out.wav`.

## Training details

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting model | Audio8-TTS-Persian (itself fine-tuned from Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B, repo commit `07e40f5`) |
| Data | central-kurdish-tts4all: ≈ 35 h of read Central Kurdish, 3 speakers (male and female audiobook narrators, male studio voice), 24 kHz, clips of 1–20 s |
| Default voice | The speaker with the most audio is trained without a reference clip; the other speakers always with a same-speaker reference, which teaches voice cloning |
| Text normalization | Sorani rules: Arabic yeh/kaf → Kurdish forms, ھ → ه, heh + ZWNJ → ە, diacritics and ZWNJ removed, numbers spelled out in Kurdish |
| Trainable parameters | Both DualAR branches (slow + fast AR), all 601M parameters |
| Optimizer | 8-bit AdamW, lr 3e-5, cosine schedule, 3% warmup, grad-norm clip 1.0 |

- **Three speakers, read speech.** Voice variety and prosody are limited; conversational speech and unseen voices are weaker.

- **Spelling follows the dataset**: the model learns pronunciation from how the transcripts are written; non-standard spellings and Latin-script words may be mispronounced.

# ampixa/audio8-nepali-wave3-onnx

Nepali zero-shot voice-cloning TTS for CPUs, packaged for ONNX Runtime with no PyTorch dependency. It is the model the [Astadhwani](https://github.com/Ampixa/astadhwani) desktop app downloads on first launch.

- **Checkpoint:** Audio8 Nepali "wave 3" final. Source checkpoint sha256 `73e1c13471213620b4b258c9cd1ebda528925f09b8599924160ed5b0c41f8dbb`. The full-precision weights are not published here.
- **Base model:** [Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b), by Audio8, under the Audio8 Community License v1.0 (`LICENSE`).
- **Runtime:** the graphs use the interface of Audio8's official 0.1B INT8 ONNX release ([Edge0/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8)). They run with the [0.1B INT8 ONNX runtime](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/onnx_runtime_0_1b_int8).
- **Sibling:** [ampixa/audio8-nepali-dpo-onnx](https://huggingface.co/ampixa/audio8-nepali-dpo-onnx) is preference-tuned. It is more accurate on content and voice match but scores lower on SCOREQ/UTMOS naturalness (see below).

## Files
| File | What | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| `slow_ar_int8.onnx` (+`.data`), `fast_ar_int8.onnx` (+`.data`) | Slow and fast AR, INT8 | **This checkpoint.** Weights swapped into the official graphs. |
| `codec_decoder_fp16.onnx` (+`.data`), `registration/codec_encoder_fp16.onnx` (+`.data`), `tokenizer/`, `config.json` | Codec (byte-identical to the base model's `codec.pth`), tokenizer, metadata | Unchanged from the official ONNX release |
| `runtime_manifest.json` | Runtime metadata | Official release, plus this checkpoint's provenance |

Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

## Conversion and parity
The official ONNX release ships graphs but no exporter, so we kept those graphs and replaced their 901 initializers:
- Linear weights: int8, symmetric, per output channel.
- Embeddings: uint8, per tensor.
- Norms, conv bias and folded Mamba constants: float.

Applying the same procedure to the official base weights reproduces all 901 published initializers bit-exactly.

Teacher-forced parity against PyTorch fp32 used identical prompts (3 Nepali sentences × 60 steps):

| | Official base: PyTorch vs official INT8 | This checkpoint: PyTorch vs these INT8 graphs |
|---|---|---|
| Semantic logit correlation | 0.9970 | 0.9950 |
| Semantic greedy top-1 agreement | 85.0% | 98.9% |
| Acoustic logit correlation | 0.9975 | 0.9999 |
| Acoustic greedy top-1 agreement | 75.7% | 79.5% |

## Training lineage and data
1. **Wave 1:** full fine-tune of the base on YouTube conversational Nepali, 1,327 speakers, 318.8 h.
2. **Waves 2–3:** continued training on about 575 h, with benchmark sentences and voices screened out. This data includes YouTube material used under a memorandum of understanding with the channels.

**The speakers in the training data did not individually consent to voice cloning.** Do not use this model to imitate any real person without that person's consent.

## Recommended inference (used by Astadhwani)
- Temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 50.
- Text front end [Swar `frontend.normalize`](https://github.com/Naamche-Labs/swar) (MIT), which spells out numbers and English words in Devanagari.
- The whole text in one generation, with no chunking and no retries.

These are the settings of the benchmark row below.

## Benchmarks (internal head-to-head, PyTorch fp32 checkpoint, the settings above, seed 0, one take)
These are automatic scores with no listening test. Values are means, with 95% bootstrap CIs in the source report.
